summary: Structured-output buffer eviction delay causing sporadic request timeouts in JSON-mode
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent request timeouts and long-tail latency when using structured-output (JSON) streaming mode. Problem appears after ~20-60s for some requests; other requests complete normally. Impact is end-to-end timeouts surfaced to the customer application (HTTP 504 / SDK timeout).

Impact:
- Multiple failed inference calls for 10 active users at ClariFin Analytics (enterprise tenant on dedicated capacity).
- Estimated 2-5% of requests hitting timeouts during peak load window (13:00–15:00 UTC).
- Downstream data processing pipelines backpressure due to missing structured outputs.

Observed behavior:
- Request initiates, initial token stream begins as expected.
- Streaming stalls mid-response while server still reports active worker handling the request.
- After ~30–60s stall, client times out and request is marked failed. No 5xx returned from API gateway.
- Replaying identical requests in non-JSON mode (plain text) returns normally and quickly.

Hypothesis: eviction/flush of structured-output buffer or decoder finalization logic can block when certain metadata fields are present (multi-field arrays), causing long-tail stalls in the streaming decoder / postprocess step.

Notes: customer attached sample prompts and the failing request IDs in comments below.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer tenant credentials and call /v1/chat/stream with mode=structured-json and schema that includes nested arrays and 4 'metadata' fields.
2) Observe initial tokens emitted, then wait — some requests stall after emitting ~80% of tokens.
3) Re-run identical request switching to mode=plain-text; observe normal completion within expected latency.
4) Run load test with 50 concurrent streams for 5 minutes to reproduce long-tail under sustained load.
5) Collect request IDs from customer logs and cross-check with serving-runtime traces.
Sample failing request ids: req-20260310-7a2f, req-20260310-7b9c
logs: 2026-03-10T13:12:04Z srv-01 streaming-decoder INFO request=req-20260310-7a2f tokens_emitted=182 status=streaming
2026-03-10T13:12:35Z srv-01 streaming-decoder WARN request=req-20260310-7a2f stall_detected=1 last_token_timestamp=2026-03-10T13:12:05Z
Worker traces show no OOM, CPU at 45-60%, and GPU util ~30% at stall time.

2026-03-10T15:05:43Z - Samir Gupta (SRE): Acknowledged. Will collect runtime traces and enable additional debug logging on the affected dedicated pool.
2026-03-10T17:02:01Z - Marco Liu (Platform Eng): Noted similar pattern to SUP-20345 where structured-output postprocessing held a mutex during finalization; adding hypothesis to investigation.

2026-03-11T09:30:22Z - Samir Gupta (SRE): Temporarily increased decoder flush timeout and verified reduction in observed customer timeouts (from 3% to ~0.5%) during a 2-hour window. Planning a safer hotfix.

2026-03-12T11:11:09Z - Priya Patel (Customer Success): Customer confirmed they can reproduce reliably with their schema that includes arrays of metadata and trailing optional fields. They provided sample schema and data (attached in customer portal).
2026-03-13T08:44:55Z - Samir Gupta (SRE): Added link to PR with instrumentation and a candidate fix for buffer eviction race: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/812
investigation_notes: - Reproduced stall locally using customer's schema when structured-output contains nested arrays > 3 levels and > 500 total elements across fields.
- Thread dump shows streaming-decoder main loop waiting on eviction condition variable while postprocessor holds the output buffer lock for extended time.
- CPU profiling indicates a synchronous JSON serialization pass in postprocess that occasionally spikes to 500ms for large payloads; this coincides with stalls.
- Non-JSON streaming bypasses postprocess serializer; explains why plain-text mode unaffected.
- No evidence of GPU or memory pressure; issue localized to CPU-side finalization path.
- Candidate root cause: structured-output finalization path performs full in-memory JSON assembly under a global lock causing head-of-line blocking for other streams on same worker.
- Affected customers appear to be on dedicated pools with default worker concurrency=8 leading to head-of-line blocking when one request enters heavy serialization.
- Related to prior issue SUP-19862 but different trigger (large nested arrays vs. rare unicode causing decoder hang).
- Instrumentation added to measure per-request serialization time and lock hold time (PR linked above).
workaround: 1) Customer: Reduce nested array sizes or paginate metadata into separate follow-up requests.
2) Temporary server-side mitigation: lowered default worker concurrency on affected dedicated pool from 8 -> 4 to reduce contention (rolled out 2026-03-11 05:00 UTC).
3) Increased per-request streaming flush timeout to avoid client hits for 60s windows while hotfix is validated.
4) Recommend customers use plain-text mode for extremely large structured arrays until fix is released.
next_steps: - Validate PR 812 in staging with large nested-array test corpus (owner: Marco Liu) by 2026-03-14.
- If tests pass, schedule hotfix rollout to affected dedicated pools with canary at 5% traffic, monitor serialization_time metric and 504 rate.
- Postmortem to capture mitigation, RCA, and long-term design (consider async serializer and per-request buffer quotas).
- Communicate ETA to customer and propose a post-deployment verification window before closing
